text.p: Italian Btp futures pared back earlier gains as trading wound down ahead of the weekend but dealers said good support seen in the 135.50/40 area was a positive signal. The September Liffe contract ended three basis points up at 135.58 after earlier setting a new high at 135.84.
The Bund spread had also narrowed to a new 101 bps low.
"This afternoon the impetus from buying seen in the morning petered out and the Btp future saw a slight retracement, but it could start climbing again on Monday," one operator said.
The closure of U.S. markets for the Independence Day holiday affected all European debt markets, sharply reducing volumes.
In cash bonds, the February 2007 Btp gained 13 bps to 101.55 to yield 6.62 percent, after a day's high at 101.70, and the Bund spread was at 102 bps at the close.

"The 100 basis point spread target had been the goal by the end of the year but we're just about there already," one dealer said. Some said the Italian market could gain even more over Germany while others remained more cautious.

"We will remain tied to foreign markets over the next few days," one dealer said. "For the Bund it's crucial to overcome resistance at 102.60," another said, noting that it was also important to see a continuing positive trend in Treasuries.
